title: The Missing Blueprint
incident: A classified hypersonic propulsion blueprint (Project Chimera) disappeared from the CAD design terminal between 6:30 PM and 7:15 PM, hours before a Department of Defense contract presentation. The local file was deleted and an unauthorized USB flash drive transfer was detected on the network.
centralQuestions: Whose user credentials executed the unauthorized export command?
Was the physical terminal occupied by the person whose badge opened the laboratory door?
Did the network transfer originate from an internal workstation or remote VPN tunnel?
Why was the project printer queued for 40 blank pages at 6:45 PM?

timeline.event: Lead Engineer Dr. Marcus Brody locks his terminal and attends all-hands briefing.
Lab security door registers keycard swipe of Project Manager Rachel Cole.
CAD terminal logs user login under Marcus Brody's administrative credentials.
A high-speed USB 3.1 storage device is mounted on the CAD terminal.
Export of 'Chimera_Core_Rev4.cad' completed; original file permanently purged.
Rachel Cole swipes out of the engineering lab.
Dr. Brody returns to the lab and discovers the design directory empty.

suspects.name: Dr. Marcus Brody
suspects.motive: Bitter dispute over intellectual property royalties; secretly in talks with competitor.
suspects.statement: He says his password was sticky-noted inside his locked desk drawer.
relevant_evidence: His credentials were used for the export.
Desk drawer lock shows no scratch marks.
supporting_evidence: Continuous video shows him in the executive briefing from 6:00 PM to 7:10 PM.
suspicious_evidence: Had administrative authority to delete the file permanently.
suspects.uncertainty: Being in the briefing proves he did not physically type at the CAD terminal.
open_questions: Did someone steal his password or use a remote macro?

suspects.name: Rachel Cole
suspects.motive: Performance bonus tied directly to budget cuts; threatened by engineers.
suspects.statement: She says she entered the lab only to retrieve her reading glasses from her desk.
relevant_evidence: Her badge opened the door at 6:32 PM and exited at 7:00 PM.
Was inside the lab during the USB mount.
supporting_evidence: CCTV shows her holding glasses case when leaving.
suspicious_evidence: Was the only person badge-authorized inside the room during the export.
suspects.uncertainty: She does not have technical CAD administrative knowledge.
open_questions: Could she execute an automated script on Brody's terminal?

suspects.name: Devon Miller
suspects.motive: Contract expiring next month with no renewal offer; heavy consumer loans.
suspects.statement: He says he was in the server closet configuring firewall patches.
relevant_evidence: Server closet shares maintenance duct into CAD lab.
supporting_evidence: Firewall change tickets match the timeframe.
suspicious_evidence: A custom Bash automation script was uploaded to the local subnet at 6:35 PM.
suspects.uncertainty: Admin activity is standard during scheduled maintenance windows.
open_questions: Did the export happen via physical USB or network redirection?

suspects.name: Maya Lin
suspects.motive: Rejected for full-time sponsorship; academic thesis dependent on hypersonic data.
suspects.statement: She says she was in the library compiling bibliography references.
relevant_evidence: Library turnstile records her entry at 6:15 PM.
A SanDisk USB drive was found in her backpack.
supporting_evidence: Library desktop logged into her university portal.
suspicious_evidence: USB drive serial number matches the manufacturer vendor code of the mounted drive.
suspects.uncertainty: SanDisk drives are extremely common consumer items.
open_questions: Does the drive serial number match the specific OS mount log?

witnesses.name: Security Guard Henderson
witnesses.statement: No outside visitors entered the R&D wing all evening.
witnesses.limitations: Does not monitor internal lab doors directly.

witnesses.name: Dr. Aris Thorne
witnesses.statement: Brody was sitting right beside me in the briefing until 7:10 PM.
witnesses.limitations: Could not see Brody's phone or smart watch under the table.

evidence.title: Lab Ingress Access Log
evidence.description: Door reader registered Rachel Cole's badge at 6:32 PM and 7:00 PM.
evidence.establishes: Rachel Cole's badge entered and exited during the theft.
evidence.does_not_establish: That Cole operated Brody's CAD terminal.

evidence.title: USB Hardware Mount ID
evidence.description: Registry event shows USB device 'VEN_SANDISK_PRO_SN88392' mounted at 6:48 PM.
evidence.establishes: A specific serial-numbered USB drive was physically plugged into the terminal.

evidence.title: Desk Drawer Key Copy
evidence.description: A brass desk key matching Brody's locked drawer was discovered under the water cooler in the lab.
evidence.establishes: Someone duplicated or relocated Brody's desk key.

evidence.title: CAD Export Audit Record
evidence.description: Export utility launched via batch file 'auto_extract.bat' executed from the USB root directory.
evidence.establishes: The export required zero manual CAD skill; it was fully pre-programmed.

evidence.title: Printer Buffer Queue
evidence.description: 40 blank pages queued to the lab network printer at 6:45 PM.
evidence.establishes: A distraction or network test was executed.

redHerrings: Brody's credentials were used, making him look like an insider saboteur, but his executive meeting alibi is 100% verified.
Intern Maya Lin possessed a SanDisk drive, but forensic serial comparison proves her drive has serial #11429, not #88392.

hiddenSolution.explanation: Rachel partnered with competitor representatives for an executive payoff. She acquired a duplicate key to Brody's desk, retrieved his password note, entered the lab at 6:32 PM, plugged in a pre-configured auto-extraction USB drive provided by the competitor, purged the master file, and left at 7:00 PM with the drive hidden in her glasses case.
decisiveEvidence: E-D (Pre-programmed batch file requiring no CAD skill)
uncertainties: Where the USB drive was hidden after 7:00 PM
hiddenSolution.alternativeExplanation: Devon Miller executed the extraction remotely through a hijacked local loopback while Rachel was merely retrieving her glasses.

missingEvidence: Camera footage inside the private CAD lab room
Search warrant on Rachel Cole's personal vehicle
rules: Badge swipe establishes presence in the room, not operation of keyboard.
Pre-configured scripts allow non-technical suspects to perform advanced digital theft.
